summary: guru-review: bulk tag-action endpoint + per-chunk coverage to prevent silent under-queueing
description:
During the blavatsky-sd staged_tags review loop (~11k verdicts queued via individual POST /api/tags/:id/action calls from a scripted client), a client-side bug silently dropped ~863 verdicts across five batches. The API returned success for every POST it received, so the drift was invisible until the review cursor stopped matching; recovery required re-parsing the client's working scripts.

Requested changes (priority order):

1. Bulk endpoint — POST /api/tags/bulk accepting [{target_id, action}] (optionally reviewer + batched client_action_ids), returning {queued, skipped, unknown_ids}. Eliminates per-tag HTTP loops and lets client and server counts reconcile in one response.

2. Per-chunk coverage in GET /api/chunks — report pending_total vs queued per chunk so an under-queued batch is visible on the very next fetch instead of surfacing only as cursor drift batches later.

3. Reconciliation field in responses — include remaining_pending_in_text (or by-chunk coverage) in action POST responses and/or GET /api/apply/preview, making completeness checkable by comparison rather than by reconstructing intent from client-side files.

4. Documented pattern for scripted bulk review — recommend a JSONL working file ({target_id, action, why}) as source of truth, uploaded by a simple reader script, rather than constructing payloads inline in code where dropped lines are silent.
